title: Execution Hint Orchestrator: token-phase aware autotuner for kernel hints
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: kernel selection today is dominated by static heuristics keyed only to architecture and max-seqlen buckets. This misses per-request token-phase dynamics (early prefill vs late decode), short-burst conversational patterns, and KV cache hit variance. As a result we pay unnecessary cost on tail latency and use suboptimal kernels for many realistic conversational traces.

Goal: build an "Execution Hint Orchestrator" (EHO) that produces lightweight, per-request kernel hints using a token-phase aware autotuner. Hints are low-cost signals (suggested kernel family, prefill/decode routing flag, expected KV-hit bucket) attached to requests and consumed by the kernel routing layer. The autotuner refines hint mappings online using safe, bandit-style updates and microbench feedback.

Success metrics (target within 6 weeks of rollout):
- 5-12% reduction in p95 token-latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads on dedicated pools (measured per-model).
- 3-7% reduction in average per-token GPU cost across mixed conversational traffic.
- No more than 0.5% increase in correctness/regression alerts (quality tests) attributable to kernel switching.

Approach summary:
1) Offline profiling: extend microbench harness to measure kernel families across arches for representative token-phase slices (initial prefill frames, mid-sequence region, tail decode frames) and KV-hit ratios. Produce a canonical "token-phase x arch" performance table.
2) Lightweight runtime probe: implement token-phase classifier that tags requests into phases (prefill | steady | decode-tail) using message-length, user-turn features, and first-n token dynamics. Classifier runs in <50us.
3) Hint generator: combine classifier output + per-customer profile + cached profile lookups to emit kernel hints. Hints are compact strings consumed by e.g., router: "kfam=matmul64_quant;mode=prefill;kv=high".
4) Online autotune: a safe bandit (epsilon-greedy with per-arch safety bounds) evaluates alternative kernel families by shadowing a small % of traffic and consuming microbench telemetry. Loss function mixes latency, cost and correctness safety penalties.
5) Rollout & fallback: hints are advisory — router can override based on capacity. Implement conservative default maps and automatic rollback if SLAs deviate.

Why token-phase: many kernels have different strengths depending on phase (e.g., kernels with aggressive prefill packing vs decode-optimized microkernels). Token-phase aware mapping unlocks dynamic gains without heavy per-request model switching cost.
acceptance_criteria:
- Token-phase classifier integrated into request pipeline and exposes phase tag on 99% of requests in test traffic.
- Hint format spec documented and validated with Console & router teams.
- Autotuner runs in canary mode on 2 dedicated pools, evaluates at least 3 kernel families per arch, and reports metrics to runtime telemetry dashboard.
- Rollout plan with automated rollback triggers (latency p99 rise, error-rate increase, cost spike) documented and rehearsed.
- PRs merged for profiling harness, classifier, hint generator, and router consumer.
tasks: Design token-phase taxonomy and classifier features (Aisha)
Extend microbench harness for phase-sliced profiling (Ben)
Spec hint payload and router contract (PM review)
Implement hint generator & cache layer in runtime router (Ben)
Build online bandit autotuner and safety controller (Infra team assist)
Create telemetry dashboards and per-model KPI reports (Observability)
Canary rollout to small dedicated cluster and collect 2 weeks of data
QA: run eval prompt sets to ensure quality remains stable
notes: Trade-offs discussed in design review: keep hints advisory to minimize risk, avoid per-request kernel swaps except where cost/latency wins exceed safety threshold. We prefer conservative epsilon-greedy exploration over aggressive Thompson sampling to simplify rollback. Decided to start with 3 kernel families per arch (fast-prefill, balanced, decode-optimized).
